leaves.note: Late September is early autumn in Berlin. The German Weather Service's phenological year puts the colouring of the leaves at the start of late autumn, two seasons later, so the trees along the course are in leaf on race day and a crown is about as thick as the city's register describes it.

difficulty_model.description: Energy cost of running at this grade divided by the cost on flat ground (1.0 = flat; 1.5 = 50% more energy per meter). Valid for grades from -45% to +45%.

sources.title: Berlin Marathon 2025 course file (GPX)
sources.licence: Course geometry of public roads (facts only; file not redistributed)

sources.title: ATKIS® DGM – Digital terrain model 1 m (Geoportal Berlin)
sources.note: Bare-earth heights in DHHN2016; feed updated 2025-12-18.

sources.title: ATKIS® DOM – Digital surface model 1 m (Geoportal Berlin)
sources.note: Surface heights (ground plus buildings, vegetation and bridges), same grid and tiling as DGM1; feed updated 2025-08-07, tiles from a 2021 flight. Used only for bridge decks.

sources.title: Earth Gravitational Model 2008 (EGM2008), 2.5-minute worldwide geoid height grid (U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency)
sources.licence: Public domain: a work of a U.S. federal agency, labelled so in the file and by the PROJ project that redistributes it (NGA's own page states no terms)
sources.note: How far sea level is above the WGS84 ellipsoid. Added to each height above sea level to get the height the 3D scene needs. Read from https://cdn.proj.org/us_nga_egm08_25.tif (a GeoTIFF the PROJ project made from the model), between the four grid points around each place. Against the cities' official models it is 0.21 m high in Berlin (GCG2016) and about 0.37 m high in New York (GEOID18 and the step from NAD83 to WGS84).

sources.title: Gebäudehöhen 2022 (Umweltatlas Berlin, map 06.10.1), from the city's LoD2 3D building models
sources.note: Ridge height (Firsthöhe) above the ground, on the building outlines of the ALKIS cadastre, worked out from Berlin's LoD2 3D building models and published for 2022. Read only along the course corridor. A block is as tall as its ridge, so under a pitched roof it stands a little proud of the eaves. Buildings the city could work out no height for are not drawn.

sources.title: Baumbestand Berlin: the city's register of its street trees and park trees (Geoportal Berlin)
sources.note: One record per tree, with its species, its height (baumhoehe) and the width of its crown (kronedurch), read along the course corridor as WFS. The register covers the street trees and part of the trees in public green spaces, so a wood the city does not tend is not in it. Each crown stands on the city's own bare-earth model; where the register gives no crown width it is taken as 0.6 of the tree's height, the register's own median, and where a crown starts is worked out, never measured (PLAN.md D60).

sources.title: NOAA Solar Calculator (US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration): the equations for the sun's position
sources.licence: Work of the US government: public domain
sources.note: Geometric position, without the bending of light near the horizon: what casts a shadow.
